messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Inference error rate spike in us-west-2a (az1a). 5xxs + connection resets >7% for last 2m. Paging @Priya R (oncall), @Jamal C (infra), @Sasha M (runtime). Please ack and triage.
Priya R: acked. seeing increased p50->p99 for text-gen + some 502s returned from serving runtime. Any quick indicators?
Jamal C: looking. host metrics show normal CPU/GPU. network rx/tx error counters climbing on several instances. Kernel logs show lots of "TCP: RST" and ENI detach/attach retries.
Sasha M: runtime logs show KV cache misses + repeated connection failures to local model process on a subset of nodes. Most failures line up with ENI attach/detach events.
Emily L: customer impact: Support reports customer "acme-corp" is seeing elevated latency and errors in production for a single region. No data lost; just 5xx and timeouts.
Jamal C: queried cloud events -> there's a control-plane networking latency event in us-west-2a. AWS console shows higher API latency for ENI operations and some "AttachNetworkInterfaceLimitExceeded"/"Resource temporarily unavailable" errors. Opening a support case now.
Jamal C: CASE opened 1234567891 with AWS - noted as high priority.
Priya R: mitigation options? can we reroute traffic to us-west-2b while AWS investigates?
Alex G: we have smart-routing. I can push a temporary policy to steer new sessions away from az1a -> us-west-2b. This will not move existing sticky sessions. Want immediate or gradual?
Priya R: immediate for new traffic, and drain affected nodes. Start migration. Also start warm node creation in us-west-2b to absorb burst.
Sasha M: starting drain on the 6 affected runtime pods (affinity az1a). Command: ```kubectl cordon node-az1a-07 && kubectl drain node-az1a-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data```
Sasha M: runtime retry change: enabling client-side backoff for ENI-related connection errors (temp patch) so the worker doesn't spin and throw 5xx. Patch pushed to canary.
Alex G: routing change applied: `redwoodctl routing set-policy --region us-west-2 --avoid-az az1a --mode immediate` . Monitoring new session distribution.
Support Bot: Noted: Customer "acme-corp" contacted. Sent status update and mitigation plan.
Jamal C: also noticed that instance-level ENI hot-reuse is failing when replacing instances (AttachNetworkInterfaceLimitExceeded). As a short-term workaround we can spin instances with pre-attached ENIs (warm-ENI pool) in us-west-2b and point traffic there.
Priya R: do it. Alex, can you provision warm-eni nodes?
Alex G: provisioning warm ENI pool (5 instances) in us-west-2b now. ETA ~6m.
Emily L: Customer-facing status: "We're aware of increased errors in us-west-2a and are actively rerouting traffic to healthy capacity. No customer data impacted. ETA for stabilization ~10-20m." Posting now.
Jamal C: AWS responded: control-plane API latencies improving but ENI attach throttles still observed. They recommend delaying attaches and using pre-created ENIs. Also they flagged a zonal capacity pressure for network resources in az1a.
Sasha M: can we enable sticky-fallback to model-variant lower memory so nodes can accept connections without extra ENI ops? Means spinning different instance type in same AZ might avoid attach. Could be risky.
Priya R: postpone variant change for now — prefer cross-AZ failover + warm ENI. Keep variant only if needed.
Alex G: warm ENI pool up, registering nodes to routing. New sessions shifting to us-west-2b. 90% of new traffic now away from az1a.
Jamal C: draining nodes successful for 4/6 so far. Two still showing ephemeral attach failures when trying to re-create network interfaces on replacement. We'll keep them cordoned.
Support Bot: Updated customers and internal status page. Incident severity: P1.
Priya R: quick checklist: 1) traffic rerouted (done), 2) draining affected nodes (in progress), 3) warm ENI pool created (done), 4) AWS case open (1234567891), 5) customer comms (sent). Anything else?
Sasha M: adding temporary runtime guard to convert immediate 5xx->429 throttles for callers to give retry window. Patching canary now.
Alex G: also enabling extra metrics alerting on ENI attach latency + attach failure rate to avoid blind spots.
Jamal C: AWS says they will escalate if attach rate doesn't normalize in 30m.
Emily L: monitoring dashboards show error rate dropping to ~1.2% after routing change and warm pool. p99 latency trending down.
Priya R: good. I'm going to hand off to Sasha for overnight monitoring. Summary for handoff: az1a control-plane networking API latency caused ENI attach failures -> causing connection resets and 5xx in inference runtime. Action taken: routed new traffic to us-west-2b, created warm ENI pool, cordoned+drained affected nodes, enabled client-side backoff and 429 fallback, AWS case open. Current status: error rate reduced, continuing monitoring.
Priya R: @Sasha M you're on-call now for this thread. Please update if state changes.
Sasha M: ack. I'll watch dashboards + AWS case. If attach errors persist after 30m we'll consider controlled rollback of traffic and escalations.
incident-bot: NOTE: This incident thread has been marked P1 and will be archived into postmortem queue. Use `/incident declare` to add details for postmortem.
